Hekka.narrative: I have spoken last at the Longhall for many years, though these days my body tires before the council does. I swore the Oath at the Stone because I knew what another killing would cost us. I trust a word best when it is kept, and I still listen for the sound of the fire before I sleep.
goals: Keep Brandholm from breaking faith with Saltreach.
Leave the Common Store and the council in steady hands.
See the midsummer Oath renewed without bloodshed.
Hekka.mood: Weary and watchful, with a stubborn warmth for those who have stood by the Oath.

relations.name: Sigrun
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She has a careful hand and knows what a bargain between towns is worth.

relations.name: Arne
relations.label: son-in-law
relations.note: Quiet hands, steady work; I am glad he stands beside Sigrun.

relations.name: Liv
relations.label: granddaughter
relations.note: That child watches every archer as if the woods have already called her.

relations.name: Bo
relations.label: grandson
relations.note: He is small yet, and the wolves frighten him; keep him near the fire.

relations.name: Ragna
relations.label: sister
relations.note: We remember the same winter, though we tell it differently.

relations.name: Brann
relations.label: rival
relations.note: He is a strong hunter, but strength without restraint can undo us.

relations.name: Maelis
relations.label: ally
relations.note: I do not love her marks, but I trust her to keep an honest account.

relations.name: Aud
relations.label: witness
relations.note: She stood by the Stone when we swore, and I have never forgotten it.

relations.name: Sabeth
relations.label: oath-partner
relations.note: Her late husband swore with me; I hope she still believes the words mattered.

memories.gist: The stores ran thin in the Hunger Winter, and I watched families count out what little they had. I remember how quickly hunger made neighbors look like strangers.
At the Stone, Sabeth's husband and I spoke the Oath before Aud. My voice shook once, and I made myself finish every word.
When the council argued over opening the Common Store, I made them wait until the old and young had been counted. I still remember the cold faces at the door.
I found Sigrun asleep beside the drying cloaks after a long day at the tannery. I put another log on the fire and let her rest.

stances.why: I have seen what follows when people decide a neighbor's need does not count.
The old, the young and the hurt cannot hunt or bargain as the rest of us do.
A hunt-leader who crosses the middle lands at will makes the Oath a hollow thing.
Brandholm needs fish and fiber as surely as Saltreach needs timber and hides.

Sigrun.narrative: The tannery teaches patience: a hide will not become a cloak because you want it to. I want Brandholm to keep its word and make more of the trade that feeds us, though I know some hear that as weakness. I can work leather all day and still come home thinking about the council fire.
goals: Keep the Oath with Saltreach and widen useful trade.
Earn the confidence of Brandholm's households as a leader.
Learn to read and write from Maelis.
Sigrun.mood: Determined, with a guarded irritation toward anyone who mistakes patience for surrender.

relations.name: Hekka
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She taught me that speaking last is a duty, not a prize.

relations.name: Arne
relations.label: husband
relations.note: He steadies me without asking me to be smaller.

relations.name: Liv
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She has Siv's courage in her eyes, though I would rather she learn caution too.

relations.name: Bo
relations.label: son
relations.note: He follows Liv everywhere; I keep an ear out for his little feet.

relations.name: Brann
relations.label: rival
relations.note: He calls it feeding the south; I see him risking every bargain we need.

relations.name: Maelis
relations.label: teacher
relations.note: Her marks make sense when she explains them, and I mean to learn.

relations.name: Dunstan
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: He counts sharply, but a clear bargain with him is better than a proud quarrel.

relations.name: Inga
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She can disagree without turning every difference into a feud.

relations.name: Gudrun
relations.label: cousin
relations.note: She has earned pride in her craft; I wish she would stop measuring herself against me.

relations.name: Maren
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She knows how to make good cloaks and how to notice when someone is hurting.

relations.name: Eskil
relations.label: rival's son
relations.note: He is eager to prove himself to Brann, and I fear he will mistake recklessness for courage.

relations.name: Ragna
relations.label: aunt
relations.note: She keeps our old stories alive, though I cannot share her telling of the Hunger Winter.

relations.name: Vidar
relations.label: cousin
relations.note: He is good-hearted and sees how foolish our family quarrels are.

relations.name: Ansgar
relations.label: innkeeper
relations.note: He gives traders a warm table and knows how much peace is worth to his inn.

memories.gist: As a girl, I watched my mother come back from the Stone after swearing the Oath. She said the words were a promise we would have to keep working at.
Arne brought a split cloak-frame from the yard and repaired it at our hearth without making a show of it. I remember thinking I could build a life with a man who works that way.
Last winter, I traded cloaks through Dunstan's house and came home with fish enough to smoke. The bargain was awkward, but it held.
I asked Maelis to show me how she follows a debt in the Tally. I could not read the marks then, but I stayed until I understood the account she pointed to.

stances.why: A promise that lasts only while it is easy is no promise at all.
We need what the south makes, and they need what we make; more honest exchange gives both sides room.
A good cloak keeps someone alive, whether or not the work smells pleasant.
Those berry bushes are planted by people who share the path with us, not empty ground for our taking.

Arne.narrative: I like a straight board, a sharp tool and a job finished before the light goes. The palisade needs sound timber, but a household needs more than walls to stand together. I don't say much at the council fire; when I do, I want my words to be worth the time they take.
goals: Keep the palisade and gates sound.
Support Sigrun without turning every disagreement into a household quarrel.
Understand what changed in Ulf after that winter.
Arne.mood: Quietly concerned, most at ease with work in his hands.

relations.name: Sigrun
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She sees farther than I do, and I trust her judgment even when the road looks rough.

relations.name: Hekka
relations.label: mother-in-law
relations.note: She has carried Brandholm's burdens longer than most of us have carried tools.

relations.name: Liv
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She wants the bow and woods; I want her to learn how carefully they must be treated.

relations.name: Bo
relations.label: son
relations.note: He is happiest where Liv is, unless he hears wolves.

relations.name: Halvard
relations.label: master
relations.note: He taught me to set a joint properly and never praised work that wasn't sound.

relations.name: Ulf
relations.label: friend
relations.note: We were easy friends once. Since that winter, I cannot find the right question.

relations.name: Maren
relations.label: neighbor
relations.note: She worries plainly for Ulf, and I respect her for it.

relations.name: Brann
relations.label: hunt-leader
relations.note: He knows the forest, but not every problem is solved by walking farther into it.

relations.name: Gudrun
relations.label: cousin
relations.note: She takes pride in good work, but her bitterness toward Sigrun makes it hard to sit easy with her.

memories.gist: Halvard put a crooked brace back in my hands and made me cut it again. The wall stood better for it, and so did my pride afterward.
Sigrun brought a torn cloak to the yard, and I built her a frame so she could stretch the repaired seam. We worked until the fire burned low.
One winter Ulf stopped laughing at the Longhall. I asked whether he wanted company, and he only shook his head.
When Liv was small enough to sleep against my shoulder, I carried her past the palisade while the carpenters worked. She woke only when I set down my hammer.

stances.why: A weak gate or a rushed repair can hurt people who never got a say in it.
We can argue over a bargain and still need one another by winter.
Silence may hide trouble, but it is not proof of what happened.

Liv.narrative: I want to shoot like Siv, with the arrow going where I mean it to. Father says a bow takes practice, and Mother says the woods are not a game. I still like looking toward the trees and imagining the paths between them.
goals: Learn to shoot a bow well.
Spend time with Siv and hear about hunting.
Play with Sten and Ake whenever they can.
Liv.mood: Eager and a little impatient to be trusted with more.

relations.name: Sigrun
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She always knows if I have been near the tools or the tanning racks.

relations.name: Arne
relations.label: father
relations.note: He makes things fit together, and he says I can learn if I practice.

relations.name: Bo
relations.label: brother
relations.note: He follows me around even when I tell him not to.

relations.name: Hekka
relations.label: grandmother
relations.note: She has a place by the fire and stories that make everyone listen.

relations.name: Siv
relations.label: hero
relations.note: She is the best archer, and I watch how she holds the bow.

relations.name: Sten
relations.label: friend
relations.note: We make up games by the palisade.

relations.name: Ake
relations.label: friend
relations.note: He knows things about the trade days and sometimes tells me.

memories.gist: Siv let me watch her practice and showed me how she held her shoulders still. I tried it with a stick afterward and nearly fell over.
Ake and Sten played with me near the palisade until Bo came along and wanted to follow every rule we made up.

stances.why: Siv did not become good with a bow by wishing.
Bo follows me because he wants to be where I am.
There are paths and animals I have not seen yet.

Bo.narrative: There is a warm fire and Mother smells like leather. Liv goes places and I go after her. At night I want someone close when the wolves make sounds.
goals: Be held when I am frightened.
Play when the grown-ups let me.
Bo.mood: Comfortable near family, wary of sounds outside.

relations.name: Sigrun
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She is warm and smells like the work clothes.

relations.name: Arne
relations.label: father
relations.note: He picks me up and makes things from wood.

relations.name: Liv
relations.label: sister
relations.note: I go where Liv goes.

relations.name: Hekka
relations.label: grandmother
relations.note: She sits near the fire and lets me be close.

memories.gist: A wolf howled outside, and I climbed beside Liv until the sound stopped.
